items.title: Chester Jones Interview, 1961-07-10
items.q: The interviewee only responds to the interviewer's mention of Wilbert Tillman with 'but nobody would do anything,' indicating no personal interaction or relationship is described.

ctx.x: Well, I wouldn't say every set. I mean, maybe one or two numbers and then they'll do it, you know. I think it's according to the way the fathers was feeling if they had liked that number themselves, that particular number, when they'd do it over. But if something that didn't, you know, really, it's just like you, if you like something, a number you like, and it was time for you to go out on that number, you go out and look like you're just beginning to get that feeling that you want to play more of it. See, you…

You know, that Fulham business reminds me. When I used to go here, Joe Avery and Wilbert Tillman up at Towers, Big Garden up by Adam and Buck, I don't know if he ever said it. But they'd play a number, and they'd come to the end, and they'd stop. Now, I don't know how many, whether they'd just stop for a bar or two. And then all of a sudden, they'd start up again, and it was a way of Fulham,
